resumen: The same bridge with one leg in the air. A single glute lifts the whole hip, and you have to stop the pelvis dropping to one side.
ejecucion: Lie face up with one foot planted and that knee bent.
Extend the other leg or hold it tucked, without putting it down.
Drive through the planted heel and raise the hip until torso and thigh line up.
Both hip bones should stay level: if one drops, you have gone too high.
Lower slowly rather than dropping the hip.
matices: In the cited study of nine rehabilitation exercises, the single-leg version nearly doubled gluteus maximus activation compared with the two-leg bridge. It is the natural progression once the normal bridge stops costing anything.
